From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Oct 7, 2025 at 9:12 AM PDT
Subject: Release train: add required CI check for release note preview on model metadata changes

Chloe (cc Marissa) —

Ahead of the next release train, Release Eng wants to make one CI check *required* for any changes to model metadata (schema v1 + model/variant records):

1) Validate metadata + schema invariants (JSON Schema + our custom rules)
2) Generate a “release note preview” artifact from the metadata diff + event template mapping
3) Enforce redaction (public vs internal fields) and fail if any internal-only copy would be published

Why now:
- We’ve had multiple “silent change” escalations where the underlying model promotion happened but customer-facing notes were missing/late (SUP-28411).
- The internal notes leak incident (pr-18463 hotfix) highlighted that we need hard gates, not conventions.

Proposal (what becomes required):
- GitHub check name: “Model metadata: validate + release note preview”
- Applies when files under /model-registry/** or metadata payload fixtures change, plus any control plane changes that modify release-note templates/mapping.
- Produces two artifacts:
  - public_preview.md (exactly what Console/docs would render)
  - internal_preview.md (includes internal-only fields)
- Fails if:
  - required metadata fields missing (version, compatibility, rollout eligibility, deprecation semantics)
  - category/severity cannot be determined
  - public_preview.md contains any internal-only strings/fields
  - release note copy uses restricted language (e.g., “guarantees improved accuracy”)

Approvals / ownership:
- If the diff includes any breaking change or deprecation fields, require explicit approval from CODEOWNERS for model-metadata and Console rollouts.
- For changes marked “security” category, require additional sign-off from Security review group (we can keep this as “recommended” for MVP if needed, but I’d like it required).

Timeline:
- Dry-run (non-blocking) on Oct 10
- Blocking required check on Oct 17 for repos: redwood-model-registry + redwood (control plane)
- Docs repo follows Oct 24 once the artifact format is stable

Escalation path:
- If this blocks an urgent fix: reply in-thread or ping me directly; we can use an override label “release-note-check-override” for one-off emergencies (requires Release Eng approval + follow-up ticket).

Attached:
- ReleaseNotePreviewCheck-RFC-v0.3.pdf
- example-release-note-preview.txt

Can you sanity check the impact on your team’s workflow? Specifically: expected false positives, and whether the approval gates align with how you’re planning to ship the Console surfaces.

— Connor
Connor O'Brien
Release Engineering | Redwood Inference

From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Oct 7, 2025 at 11:03 AM PDT
Subject: Re: Release train: add required CI check for release note preview on model metadata changes

Thanks — directionally supportive.

Main concerns from Console backend side:
1) Blocking checks on Oct 17 feels aggressive given we’re mid-integration and still iterating the category mapping. If the check fails on “category cannot be determined,” that’s going to slow down a bunch of small metadata fixes.
2) We need clarity on what constitutes “breaking.” For model metadata, lots of changes are “behavioral” without being API-breaking.
3) Override label needs very tight guardrails. If it becomes the escape hatch, we’ll end up where we started.

Questions:
- Can the check be required only when a model version is being promoted (vs any metadata edit)?
- For “security” category sign-off: who is the actual approver/alias? We can’t block on a vague group.

If we can keep the gating precise, I’m fine with it.

— Chloe
Chloe Martin
EM, Console Backend | Redwood Inference

From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Oct 7, 2025 at 12:18 PM PDT
Subject: Re: Release train: add required CI check for release note preview on model metadata changes

All fair.

Re (1) category mapping: we can make “unknown category” a warning during the Oct 10–17 dry-run and only turn it into a failure on Oct 24 *except* for promotions. For promotions (i.e., “model version promoted” event) it should be hard fail—otherwise we risk publishing nothing.

Re (2) “breaking”: in the style guide + templates we’re using “breaking” only when customers must take action to maintain functional behavior:
- tokenizer change requiring re-tokenization or prompt format changes
- removed model/variant/quant profile (deprecation -> disabled)
- compatibility constraint change that invalidates pinned deployments
- changes that alter supported tool/function calling schema in a non-backward compatible way

Behavioral drift that doesn’t require action should be “quality” or “behavioral change” but not “breaking.” (Marissa: please confirm you’re aligned with this, since it impacts customer wording.)

Re (3) override label: agree. Proposed guardrails:
- Only Release Eng can apply it (or approve it via PR comment)
- Requires a linked follow-up ticket (Linear) in PR description
- Auto-posts to #eng-releases with PR link + reason
- Expires after 7 days (we remove the label and the check becomes blocking again)

Re security approver: for MVP we can route to Naomi Feldman as explicit approver (or whoever she designates) rather than a group alias. I’d rather have one name than a vague list.

On “only when promoting”: technically easiest to scope by file paths (metadata diffs). But we can also add logic that only *blocks* on promotions. We already emit “model version promoted” events in control plane; pr-18452 includes the event marker in the preview generation.

If you’re OK with that split: metadata edits = required check but non-blocking failures for category during transition; promotions = hard fail.

— Connor

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Oct 7, 2025 at 2:41 PM PDT
Subject: Re: Release train: add required CI check for release note preview on model metadata changes

Yes on the breaking definition.

Two product constraints to bake into the check/templates:
- The preview should force “customer impact” language (what changed, who is affected, how to roll back) and avoid performance/quality claims unless the metadata includes a linked eval run ID + baseline reference.
- We should treat “deprecation” as a first-class category with timeline fields (announce_at, effective_at) and block promotion if those are missing when deprecation is present.

Chloe’s point about workflow is real; I’m OK with a phased rollout as long as promotions are always gated.

— Marissa
Marissa Cole
Director of Product, Console & Rollouts | Redwood Inference

From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Oct 8, 2025 at 10:09 AM PDT
Subject: Re: Release train: add required CI check for release note preview on model metadata changes

Got it. I’ll update the rollout plan accordingly and align with the template logic.

Updated gating behavior (proposed):
A) Always run check on relevant diffs
- Generates public/internal previews
- Enforces redaction (hard fail)

B) Promotions (hard fail starting Oct 17)
- Must have category + severity
- Must include “customer impact” section fields in the metadata (who impacted, rollback guidance link)
- If deprecation present: require timeline fields (announce_at/effective_at)
- If quality/perf claim present: require eval_run_id + baseline_id (otherwise claim is stripped from public preview and the check fails if the template would have emitted it)

C) Non-promotion edits (transition period)
- Category mapping “unknown” = warning until Oct 24
- Missing optional guidance links = warning

Escalation:
- For urgent prod issues, reply-all + tag me; if I’m offline, Chloe is second approver for the override label (only for incident-class fixes). Marissa is final escalation if we have an actual product risk in blocking a fix.

I’ll also add a short “how to unblock yourself” section to the CI failure output (i.e., which fields are missing + link to style guide).

— Connor

Closing the loop with dates + next steps.

Dates:
- Oct 10: CI check lands in non-blocking mode (all repos in scope). Expect noisy warnings while we tune category mapping.
- Oct 17: “promotion = hard fail” goes live for redwood-model-registry + redwood (control plane). This is the point where a version promotion cannot merge without a clean public preview.
- Oct 24: tighten non-promotion edits (unknown category becomes failure), plus docs pipeline consumes the same artifact format.

Action items:
- Chloe: please confirm who on your side should be CODEOWNER for Console rollouts template changes (so approvals route correctly).
- Marissa: please send any final language constraints you want treated as restricted phrasing (we’ll encode them as template-level rules).

If anything blocks unexpectedly, respond here with the PR link + what you were trying to ship, and we’ll triage within the day.

— Connor
